alignments.note: Preposition rendered by *At*; the following article carries no determiner here (rule 21's determinerless clause does not arise, since the possessive is on μου).
Rule 20 proper: the genitive pronoun μου is present and free to take the supplied possessive *my*, so the article is displaced and realizes nothing.
Genitive pronoun rendered by the possessive *my*, which by rule 20 empties the article s002.
Superlative adjective to *first*; the determiner slot is already taken by *my*, so rule 58 does not arise.
Noun to *defence*, standing bare under its phrase's possessive.
Negative indefinite carrying the whole English negation; rule 17's generic-noun clause heads on *no* rather than the supplied *one*.

Dative of the person, realized by the possessive *my* inside the English idiom *took my part*. The competing reading joins μοι with παρεγένετο as one unit for the whole idiom; I split because *my* answers to the dative alone and rule 2 prefers the smallest defensible unit.

The verb is rendered by the support-verb idiom *took … part*, discontinuous around the dative's *my* under rule 15. Rule 17 heads on the meaning-bearing complement *part* rather than the light verb *took*, as *bear witness* heads on *witness*.
Substantival quantifier to *all*; no negator stands with it, so rule 87 is not in question.
Ordinary negative μή with the optative, rendered by *not*. Rule 44 is untouched, this being no interrogative particle, and no negative indefinite stands with it for rules 41 or 59.
Dative pronoun rendered by *to their*, the case preposition riding with the possessive under rules 21 and 36; the supplied noun *account* belongs to the verb's own idiom, not to the pronoun.

Optative rendered by the periphrasis *may it be laid … account*, discontinuous around *not* and *to their* under rule 15. Rule 17 and rule 91 head on *account*: the corpus glosses λογίζομαι *reckon/account*, and *laid* is the light verb the English idiom supplies. Heading on *laid* remains defensible as the finite lexical word, but rule 17 forbids choosing a word merely because it is finite.
